key: The LORD lift up His countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
s: Closing the blessing Aaron and his sons are to speak over Israel; Rashi, on 6:26, reads the lifted countenance as God suppressing His anger, and Rashbam, on 6:26, as God not hiding His face but turning to His beloved to be gracious.
src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Rashbam (Hebrew, Daat), on Numbers 6:26, Sefaria export 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.words: ישא ה' פניו אליך. יִכְבֹּשׁ כַּעֲסוֹ … ישא ה' פניו אליך - כדכתיב: ופניתי אליכם, שלא יסתיר פניו מכם. ומה שכתוב: אשר לא ישא פני איש, הקב"ה לא ישא פני איש לנקותו מכל פשעיו, אבל הוא ישא פנים שלו את אהובו שיפנה אליו לחננו
evidence.gloss: [Rashi, on 6:26, ‘the LORD lift up His countenance upon thee’:] May He suppress His anger. … [Rashbam, on 6:26, same words:] As it is written, ‘and I will turn unto you’ (Leviticus 26:9): that He will not hide His face from you. And as for what is written, ‘who regardeth not persons’, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not lift the face of a man to clear him of all his transgressions, but He lifts His own face to His beloved, to turn to him to be gracious to him.

reason: The problem holds as an editorial matter the rules can meet: the day holds the Priestly Blessing (6:24 to 26), and the current reading on 6:7 turns on nezer, crown, which the English ‘consecration’ never shows the reader, while half of it is an etymology Ibn Ezra only reports (ויש אומרים). Numbers 6:26 is a whole sentence in one unit: verse.js ok, exact, Numbers 6:26, at [122,26], 12 words. Opened packet.js tanakh 44 --verse 6:26: Rashi on ישא ה׳ פניו אליך: יכבש כעסו (may He suppress His anger; the English marks it from Numbers Rabbah 11:7, but Rashi prints and adopts it); Rashbam on the same words: He will not hide His face from you, and lifts His own face to His beloved, to turn to him to be gracious. The two genuinely differ (anger restrained against favour turned towards the beloved) and are named without resolution. Plain sense from day.js: 6:22 to 23 the LORD tells Moses to have Aaron and his sons bless Israel, 6:24 to 26 the blessing, 6:26 its last line; no four-word run from the key. The standby d044-s is on 6:27, so no clash. src names both Hebrew editions. entry-check ok.
